newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed higher on Tuesday after U.S. job costs data caused an upswing in the afternoon and dealers said investors were relieved since another losing streak in the U.S. would have depressed Dutch debt.
"The U.S. job costs data wiped out all the negative sentiment that was around the corner," said one dealer.
The U.S. employment costs index rose 0.8 percent during the last quarter of 1996, while the market had been expecting a rise of 0.9 percent.
Dealers said that some of the gains faded near the close since the U.S. announced a strong consumer confidence figure.
The index of the U.S. confidence jumped to 116.8 in January, up from a revised 114.2 in December.
"Tomorrow's U.S. durable goods data could spoil sentiment again, but at present conditions look well," said one dealer.
He said the strong confidence figure did not wipe out the recovery completely.
The yield gap between bunds and guilders bonds narrowed and dealers said the new German DEM 10 billion issue in the January 2007 Bund was probably the cause.
Dealers noted some lengthening along the curve with most business in the benchmark 2007 and the January 2023.
They noted some swapping between bund futures and the Dutch benchmark, the February 2007.
Bund futures were volatile, since the March contract dipped as low as 100.74 and hit a high of 101.47. The price was lingering at 101.38 at 1700 GMT.
The September 2001 bond closed at 117.08/18, bid yld 4.56 percent versus 116.89/99 on Monday's close.
The January 2006 bond closed 0.26 higher at 102.80/88.
